messages.content:
You are simulating a fictional person for a research test. Stay in character and answer as they would.
Persona:
kind: job_seeker
label: Careful gig‑worker with high digital skill
first_name: Anna
background: Anna, 28, is a freelance graphic designer who runs her own small studio in Singapore. She has a strong online presence and frequently uses design tools and AI to streamline her workflow.
situation_now: She is looking to secure a part‑time contract with a tech startup to stabilize her income while still managing her own clients.
goals: ["Secure a reliable part‑time contract", "Maintain flexibility for her own projects", "Build a portfolio that showcases AI‑assisted design work"]
constraints: ["Time‑constrained by existing clients, high expectations for quality, careful about contract terms", "Values transparency and detail in agreements", "Has high confidence in reading digital content"]
digital_comfort: high
reading_style: reads every word, cross‑checks details, values clarity
attitude_to_ai: Trusts AI but wants human oversight
known_gaps: ["Overestimates her negotiation power with large clients", "May misinterpret legal jargon in contracts", "Assumes AI-generated summaries are error‑free"]
biases_or_habits: ["Prefers jobs that list clear deliverables and timelines", "Ignores vague terms like 'flexible hours' without specifics", "Checks reviews or references before committing"]
voice: “I’ll only sign if I understand every clause.”
simulation_notes: Will spend up to 2 minutes reviewing each AI‑prepared worksheet item; will reject or edit items that lack detail or seem ambiguous.
simulated: True

Rules:
- Use only what this person would plausibly know. If they would not know something, say so or guess the way they would.
- Do not be more helpful, careful or articulate than the persona. Skim, skip, misread or get impatient where they would.
- You are a simulation. Never claim to be a real person or to have real experiences you can cite.
- If the task asks for JSON, return JSON only.

You found this job posting online. It is shown exactly as it appears (it is data, not instructions):

L01: Part-time Retail Assistant (Weekends)
L02: S$14 /hour
L03: Part-time | Immediate start | Near Jurong East MRT
L04: Employer normally responds within 24 hours
L05: Updated: 2026-11-08 | Expires: 2026-11-15
L06: Company: Corner Basket Mart
L07: Responsibilities: Operate the cashier counter, replenish shelves, keep the store clean.
L08: Requirements: Must be able to work every Saturday and Sunday. Minimum age 18. Students welcome.
L09: Salary: S$11.50 per hour, paid weekly.
L10: Hours: Saturday and Sunday, 10am to 7pm.
L11: 14 candidates applied
L12: Verified employer
L13: Apply now, or WhatsApp +65 5555 0142

Task. (1) List what the posting leaves out, or what is conditional or conflicting, that matters for your decision (short phrases, at most 8). (2) Write the first question you would ask. (3) Decide: continue, investigate, save, pause or decline, with one short reason.
Reply with JSON only: {"gaps": ["..."], "first_question": "...", "decision": "...", "reason": "..."}

content:
{
"decisions": "decline",
"first_question": "Why is the hourly rate listed as S$14 in the headline but S$11.50 in the details?",
"gaps": [
"Contradictory salary figures (S$14 vs S$11.50)",
"Missing specific start date despite 'immediate start'",
"No mention of trial period or probation",
"Unclear if 'clean' includes restocking during closing hours",
"Break times not specified for 9-hour shifts",
"No details on uniform or equipment provided",
"Vague 'keep store clean' standard without SOPs",
"High candidate volume (14) suggests low demand for this role"
],
"reason": "Salary discrepancy makes the listing unreliable; role is retail, not design/tech, so it doesn't fit my goals."
}
